title: Kinesiology: Muscle & Motor Development
instructions: Match each term with its correct definition. You may drag terms, tap a term and then tap a target, or use the accessible dropdown mode.

items.definition: An increase in the size of existing muscle fibers through the accumulation of myofilaments and myofibrils.
An increase in the total number of individual muscle fibers.
The basic functional contractile unit of myofibrils, added longitudinally at the muscle-tendon junction during growth.
The development of a myelin sheath around nerve fibers, essential for rapid electrical conduction and motor skill execution.
A primary male androgenic hormone responsible for pubertal muscle mass expansion and bone growth.
A specialized cell dedicated to the synthesis and storage of fat mass.
The anatomical region where muscle fibers attach to tendon tissue, serving as the site for longitudinal sarcomere addition during growth.
The total body mass composed of non-fat components, including skeletal muscle, bone, organs, and water.
The outer layer of neural tissue in the brain involved in higher-level motor control, perception, and cognition.
The propagation of electrical action potentials along nerve axons to stimulate muscle contraction.
